The cold-build and continuous dirty-scale studies currently live on separate reviewed branches. Their shared driver and Rust protocol code need one source that preserves both contracts and can pass the unchanged normal CI before integration into `main`.

This PR integrates the reviewed payload/cell-witness source from #193, the cold protocol from #189, and the explicit wide dirty-plan protocol from #194. The initial merge preserves the non-overlapping donor edits and existing review artifacts. Follow-up repairs address the exact Rust formatter hunk and the two existing Rust modules omitted by the wide build's sparse checkout.

## Resulting behavior

- Cold samples retain two fresh A/B full builds and all fifteen canonical-table comparisons. The original cold study remains bound to source `044c008c9459cfa61e7701db2eb868342c508a39`, run `37954851017`, attempt 1.
- The explicit `scale_wide_dirty_v1` profile uses a 4096/1024 main work plan. The existing `scale_capacity_v1` plan remains 200/1024, and product defaults remain unchanged. Both preserve the separate 8/128 fanout plan, incomplete-build closure, full controls and parity checks.
- The wide workflow installs the required rustfmt component and includes the two actual external Rust test modules in its build checkout. Its registered five scales × N30 population, worker deadline, output limit and concurrency remain unchanged.
- Existing failure records, old source identities, validators and TODO dependencies remain intact. No original TODO is marked complete here.

## Review and verification

The source commit is `58a890857a6b6c2da874491817beb6d561897a9a`. Independent review commit `b39fdd8c858755d1a92c176efc5340907f4a3757` covers 1095 product inputs, 75 BASE differences and 146 validation inputs. Its canonical report is `artifacts/checkpoints/p8-cold-wide-startup-integration-bfcc-20261009/independent-source-review.json`.

This PR head `34dc4e14dc96d077eae6173ab6885370323eff3f` has that review as its sole parent and changes exactly the two source-binding files. The six registry fields and four guard pins were independently checked against the actual source/review and the computed tree.

The original 44 scale-driver and 12 cold-driver Python controls actually passed on the five-file PCW2 projection (`da6289df86dd228e810a63b90f4be03c34b8d21b`), with no skipped tests and unchanged inputs before/after. Those five files are byte-identical in the final source; their execution identity is retained. This is not a claim that the final source's native Rust tests or whole CI have already passed.

An additional CI step was proposed and rejected because the original v15 verifier requires the original CI file. The final source restores that file exactly; neither the verifier nor any test threshold was relaxed.

## Open acceptance work

This remains Draft while the final source's actual normal CI and source guards run. The earlier #193 check failed the original warm-index fixture at 556.28 ms against the unchanged 500 ms limit; its failure remains recorded. Both earlier wide startup failures also remain recorded and contributed zero measurements. The repaired wide study is separately bound to `008f1ec0ae16b9b6aff9f20d033b17b2219168f8`, run `37982220020`, attempt 1.

The original G8 full study has accepted 4/150 shards and 41/1500 samples; the cold study's last declared intake is 16/150, of which 10 have published original custody. Installer ownership checks could claim user commands containing `codecortex`, delete neighboring user hooks, or report malformed configuration removal as success. The first archive publisher could overwrite a pointer created by another writer after its initial check. Unchanged index scans also retained an owned action entry for every unchanged file.

## Changes

- Match Claude Code hooks by exact owned command and event shape, preserve neighboring commands, and validate configuration before changing other files.
- Reject malformed generic JSON installer sections and preserve bytes when uninstall has nothing to remove.
- Publish an initially absent archive `latest` pointer with create-if-absent semantics; retain existing-owned pointer update behavior.
- Keep only add/update/dirty-resolution actions in the scan action map, with scanned-path membership representing unchanged files. Existing scan, hashing, resolver, resource, and admission budgets remain in force.

The product commit changes exactly eight Rust source/test files and two Python validation files. A separate independent source review inventories all 1,096 product inputs and 142 validation inputs. The final admission commit changes only the four v15 source/review pins and its registry. Existing approval algorithms, historical snapshots, CI selection, and source exclusions remain unchanged.

## Validation and limits

Focused regressions passed on their recorded reviewed sources, including 56 installer unit tests, five installer CLI tests, 42 archive-publication tests, and 36 distinct index planning/reconciliation tests. Independent reviewers additionally checked ownership, failure preservation, first-publication races, and dense/sparse action equivalence. These executions retain their original source identities; identical product bytes are not described as a new execution on this PR head.

Prior integration validation passed formatting, workspace clippy, compilation of default targets, 421 P8 Python tests, the completed remaining Rust targets, and the named fixture/corpus test. Two unchanged default runtime tests failed in the local execution environment and are not waived. The complete historical source proof is also locally blocked by two unavailable original binary Git inputs. Ordinary GitHub CI on the final PR head is required before merge.

No full-build performance improvement, full-scale acceptance, original TODO completion, or release certification is claimed. The sparse-action measurements concern only that component.

## Original TODO accounting

The original ledger remains 192 total: 163 done, 16 in progress, 12 todo, and one blocked; 29 remain. This PR contributes four scoped fixes and claims zero newly completed original TODOs. P8-005 full-scale evidence still gates the next original acceptance sequence. No existing expensive study is duplicated or dispatched by this PR workflow.
